Conducting scholarship that is mutually beneficial for the university scholar and for the community is encouraged and 
supported by the Provost Office and Leduc Center for Civic Engagement. To facilitate this, the   Engaged Scholarship/ 
Creative Activities (ESCA) Grant Program   was developed. 
Funded grants focus on engaged scholarship. “ Engaged scholarship can be defined as scholarly activities focused on 
the social, civic, economic, educational, artistic, scientific, environmental, and cultural well-being of people and places 
beyond the academy. It involves the creation and dissemination of new knowledge to address social issues through 
collaborative relationships and shared activity between those in the university and those outside the university ” 
(Campus Compact, 2022). 
The goals of the program are: 
•   Have immediate impact on a community-identified problem, need, or opportunity, with the potential for longer 
term impact; 
•   Build the capacity of the community partner organization, leading to increased effectiveness; 
•   Advance the faculty members research, scholarship, or professional activities 
•   Lead to competitive proposals for sponsored research or recognition in the applicant’s discipline or profession; 
•   Provide new opportunities for UMass Dartmouth students to advance their education and training.
